speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe exactly how your right leg was positioned when you arrived at the hospital after the collision, and do you feel any numbness or tingling in your foot?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Regarding your right leg positioning: does it feel like the knee is bent sharply forward and the foot is turned outward, or is the leg straightened out against your resistance? Also, have you lost any sensation in the top of your foot or your big toe?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The classic "shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated" position following a rear-end collision is pathognomonic for this injury. Please remain still while I prepare for a closed reduction and request an urgent Pelvis_XRay and CT_Scan to confirm the fracture status of the femoral head and acetabulum.
